title: In War, Trump and Putin Are Much Alike
gist: Keir Giles argues Trump's war on Iran has been a strategic windfall for Russia (higher oil and fertilizer revenue, suspended oil sanctions, depleted Western munitions, diverted attention from Ukraine) while the U.S. has emulated Russian ways of war and suffered a self-inflicted defeat that hands Iran control over Hormuz flows and erodes U.S. credibility with allies.

insights.claim: The oil-price surge from the Strait of Hormuz closure flipped Russia's expected 2026 budget deficit into a predicted surplus by March, undercutting early-2026 forecasts that economic strain would force Putin to scale back the Ukraine war.
insights.speaker: Keir Giles
insights.so_what: High oil prices extend Russia's war-financing runway; lowers odds of a near-term Ukraine settlement.
